html:
The world headquarters of the Theosophical Society, moved in 1882 to Adyar, on the edge of Madras (now Chennai) in south India.

The society was founded in New York in 1875 by Helena Blavatsky, Henry Steel Olcott and others. It taught that all religions share a hidden ancient wisdom, and it drew heavily on Hindu and Buddhist ideas. Moving to India made it a bridge: it brought Western people to Indian religions, and it gave educated Indians pride in their own traditions at a time when missionaries scorned them. Olcott also helped the Buddhist revival in Ceylon, where he worked with Anagarika Dharmapala.

Under Annie Besant, president from 1907, the society turned political. Besant started a Home Rule League in 1916 and became president of the Indian National Congress in 1917. She also raised the young Jiddu Krishnamurti as a coming "World Teacher", a role he gave up in 1929. Many early nationalists passed through Theosophy. The Adyar campus, with its huge banyan tree, is still the society's centre.
